# [Baseline] - WIN - D - Windows Hello for Business Disabled

Turns Windows Hello for Business off on shared devices: no PIN or biometrics per user per device. Users sign in with a FIDO2 security key or through web sign-in.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | Own baseline — PassportForWork CSP, UsePassportForWork = false. For shared devices Microsoft recommends FIDO2 security keys instead of Windows Hello for Business. |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_Hello_for_Business_Disabled.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Windows_Hello_for_Business_Disabled.json) |

> Belongs on SEC-Shared-Devices, together with [Baseline] - WIN - D - Security Key Sign-in: without that second policy users only have web sign-in on the device. Not next to [Baseline] - WIN - D - Windows Hello for Business Multi User or [Baseline] - WIN - D - Windows Hello for Business on the same device: the same setting with a different value is a Conflict. The latter is in phase 2 on the pilot group; do not put shared devices in SEC-Baseline-Pilot, and exclude SEC-Shared-Devices as soon as it moves to phase 1. [Baseline] - WIN - U - Windows Hello for Business turns WHfB on per user; which of the two wins when a user with that policy signs in on a shared device is something to test in the pilot. [Baseline] - WIN - D - Passwordless sets the PIN as the default sign-in option; without WHfB the user picks the key or web sign-in under Sign-in options the first time.
